title: Canonical degree-zero cohomology comparison with open sections
statement: For a ringed space $X$ and an open $U$, let $\Gamma_U$ denote the additive open-sections functor and $H^0_U$ its zeroth right-derived functor [def-sc-open-module-cohomology]. Define the canonical natural isomorphism $c_U:H^0_U\simeq\Gamma_U$ as rightDerivedZeroIsoSelf. The functor $\Gamma_U$ preserves finite limits. For every coefficient morphism $f:M\to N$, $c_{U,N}H^0_U(f)=\Gamma_U(f)c_{U,M}$.

source.place: Tag 01DZ, equation cohomology-modules and zeroth derived functor

proof.text: Unfold the open-sections functor into forgetting a module sheaf, forming its underlying presheaf, and evaluation. The Mathlib limit-preservation instances compose to show preservation of finite limits.
Use the existing enough-injectives instance and Functor.rightDerivedZeroIsoSelf for this left exact additive functor. Its naturality square is the displayed coefficient identity.
